title: Tell the cashier at once when the link is not signed on

blocks.text: A small merchant site runs the checkout client of unit c4 on a single link: one QMUX, no pool. The host restarted at 03:10, the adaptor reconnected a few seconds later, and until the sign-on manager got through, every purchase went to the host and came back declined. The merchant would rather tell the cashier "host unavailable" straight away and keep the card for a second try.

`CheckoutClient.authorize` in `src/main/java/com/example/practice/CheckoutClient.java` already asks `signedOn()` before it sends anything. Write `signedOn()`. The client gets the same Space as the sign-on manager, and the constructor has already worked out the two entry names you need. Two or three lines.
The tests run a real QMUX against a host that approves everything, and they play the adaptor and the sign-on manager themselves by writing to the Space.

cases.says: on a link signed on for its current connection the purchase goes to the host and is approved
a connection that is up but not signed on carries nothing, so a connected link is not enough
a sign-on belongs to the connection it was made on; a mark left by an earlier connection does not count
connections are told apart by the ready object itself, so an equal Date from a new connection is still a new connection
with the link down and no marks at all, nothing is sent: two missing entries are not a match

origin.section: 11.4 A Pool Uses a Link Only While It Is Signed On

concepts: A host that wants a sign-on declines or drops traffic on a new connection until it gets one, while isConnected() is already true.
With check-enabled a pool uses a link only while its enabled mark is the very ready object, so a client without a pool must make the same identity check before it sends.
